hints.junior: The staging build and the production build are actually two different files — the env var was different each time the build command ran.
hints.mid: This breaks "build once, promote everywhere" — redeploying the exact same files to production still points at whatever URL was baked in during the original build.
hints.staff: import.meta.env and DefinePlugin are text-substitution tools by design, not runtime config systems — the tool works exactly as documented, the mismatch is what it's being asked to do.

hints.junior: Switch "Deployed to" between Staging and Production and watch what the API URL actually does in each mode.
hints.mid: The Build ID never changes in either mode — it's the same bundle both times, only whether it produces the right backend differs.
hints.staff: Broken mode's API URL is a build-time constant baked into the bundle — switching the environment label doesn't touch the actual value the code holds.

hints.junior: A small config.json fetched once at app boot holds the environment-specific values, so the exact same built JS runs everywhere.
hints.mid: Window-injected config works too — the HTML shell sets a global before the app's script runs, since the shell (unlike the JS bundle) gets templated per deploy anyway.
hints.staff: This buys a single build that's byte-for-byte identical across every environment — what got verified in staging is provably the same code running in production.

hints.junior: There's a brief window before config.json resolves where the app doesn't know its own API URL yet — the boot sequence has to account for that.
hints.mid: Code that used to read import.meta.env at module scope has to be refactored to read from a config object threaded through app init instead.
hints.staff: config.json needs the opposite caching behavior from the rest of the bundle — fetched fresh every boot, never cached the way the content-hashed JS/CSS is.

sections.junior: Today's case is about a build that gets promoted from staging to production, files unchanged, that still quietly talks to the wrong backend.
sections.mid: An environment variable read at build time gets baked into the bundle as a literal string, so redeploying the same files elsewhere doesn't change what they actually do.
sections.staff: These build-time tools exist to let a minifier eliminate dead code for a given environment. Using them for config that needs to vary per deploy target is asking a compile-time tool to solve a runtime problem.

sections.junior: The fix is a small file, fetched once when the app starts, that holds whatever's different about this particular environment.
sections.mid: That moves the question of which environment this is from build time to boot time, which is the point where the answer is actually knowable.
sections.staff: The real win is a single built artifact that's identical everywhere, so what was verified in staging is provably the same code running in production.

sections.junior: Try switching the deployed environment in both modes and watch whether the API address actually follows along.
sections.mid: Notice the build identifier stays exactly the same in both modes. It's the same code either way, only the outcome differs.
sections.staff: In the broken mode, the label changes but the underlying constant never does. That's the whole bug in one interaction.

sections.junior: Env vars read at build time get frozen into the bundle — the same build can't move to a different environment without a rebuild.
sections.mid: Fetch environment-specific config at boot instead, so one built artifact runs correctly everywhere.
sections.staff: Runtime config isn't free. Code assuming synchronous env access needs refactoring, and the config file itself must never be cached the way the rest of the build is.
